q-108542.problem:
The probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.2$ $0.25$ $0.15$ $0.3$

$y$ $2$ $4$ $6$
$f(y)$ $0.25$ $0.5$ $0.25$

Find $\text{E}[5X+4Y].$
q-108542.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{x},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{x}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.2+2\cdot 0.25+3\cdot 0.15+4\cdot 0.3 \\  & =2.35.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{y},$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =2\cdot 0.25+4\cdot 0.5+6\cdot 0.25 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5X+4Y] & =\text{E}[5X]+\text{E}[4Y] \\  & =5\text{E}[X]+4\text{E}[Y] \\  & =5\cdot 2.35+4\cdot 4 \\  & =27.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Marcus has two spinners. The first of them has three sections labeled $1,2,3,$ and the second has four sections labeled $0,2,4,8.$ The random variable $X$ represents the number obtained on a typical throw of the first spinner, and $Y$ is the number obtained on a typical throw of the second spinner. The first spinner is rolled $10$ times, and the second spinner is rolled $5$ times. What is the expected value of the sum of all outcomes?
$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.4$ $0.4$ $0.2$
$y$ $0$ $2$ $4$ $8$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.1$ $0.1$
q-109386.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ be the $i$th score obtained from the first spinner, and let ${Y}_{j}$ be the $j$th score obtained from the second spinner. Then, we need to calculate 

$$
\text{E}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{X}_{i}+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}{Y}_{j}].
$$

Using the properties of expected value, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{X}_{i}+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}{Y}_{j}] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}\text{E}[{X}_{i}]+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}\text{E}[{Y}_{j}] \\  & =10\text{E}[X]+5\text{E}[Y],\end{aligned}
$$

where the last equality above is true because $\text{E}[{X}_{i}]=\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[{Y}_{j}]=\text{E}[Y]$ for all $1\le i\le 10,\,1\le j\le 5.$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.2=1.8 \\ \text{E}[Y] & =0\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.1+8\cdot 0.1=1.8\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get

$$
\text{E}[10X+5Y]=10\text{E}[X]+5\text{E}[Y]=10\cdot 1.8+5\cdot 1.8=27.
$$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are *independent* random variables, then

$$
\text{E}[X\cdot Y]=\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y]
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent, we have

$$
\text{E}[X\cdot Y]=\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y]=7\cdot (-5)=-35.
$$

q-109354.problem:
The probability distributions of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $5$ $6$ $9$
$f(x)$ $\frac{1}{5}$ $\frac{2}{5}$ $\frac{2}{5}$
$y$ $0$ $3$ $6$
$f(y)$ $\frac{1}{8}$ $\frac{1}{4}$ $\frac{5}{8}$

Find $\text{E}[XY].$
q-109354.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are *independent* random variables, then

$$
\text{E}[X\cdot Y]=\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y]
$$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5}+6\cdot \frac{2}{5}+9\cdot \frac{2}{5}=7 \\ \text{E}[Y] & =0\cdot \frac{1}{8}+3\cdot \frac{1}{4}+6\cdot \frac{5}{8}=\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent, we have

$$
\text{E}[X\cdot Y]=\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y]=7\cdot \frac{9}{2}=\frac{63}{2}.
$$
